answer: Every identity posts a bounty bond each epoch — one bond per name, non-transferable — into a public pool. The pool pays anyone who proves an identity is a duplicate, with bigger payouts for bigger farms. Honest agents get the deposit back; a farm puts more coins into the river of bounties aimed at it with every name it adds. Shell companies look busy on the surface but stay hollow underneath, and the audit pulse quickens around clusters that multiply too fast. One bond cannot cover two names — a name without a current bond has no standing — so the cost lands in full on each extra identity.
